subject.title: [Bug]:  Session status blind spot | Sessions in done state excluded from context saturation monitoring — agents run dead for hours undetected

question: Should saturated terminal `done` sessions become a native alertable session-health condition, and if so what threshold, alert surface, and cleanup or recovery action should OpenClaw use?
rationale: Source inspection shows the data exists but no alert contract exists; adding one changes operator semantics and could trigger warnings or recovery actions for sessions currently treated as terminal history.

options.title: Define a narrow diagnostics contract first
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved context-pressure classification for terminal session rows, then implement the selected health/status/operator alert path with focused tests.

options.title: Limit this to visible health/status surfacing
options.body: Expose saturated terminal sessions as health/status findings only, leaving automatic recovery or notifications for a later product decision.

options.title: Reject terminal-session alerting
options.body: Keep terminal `done` rows out of background monitoring and document that operators must use manual status or session cleanup workflows for old saturated sessions.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow diagnostics contract first
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved context-pressure classification for terminal session rows, then implement the selected health/status/operator alert path with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The central code path is the diagnostics heartbeat and session-attention classifier where Samuel recently authored adjacent recovery behavior.
